officialOwnShare.definition: Share of all citations attributed to your own brand's official sites. The own-site set follows the current brand scope (permissions + filters); for projects it resolves as configured owned bases → project domain → brand×country catalog — the same judgment as the dashboard official-site citation KPI. The Official (HMG) slice in the source-category chart counts every HMG official site, so the two can differ.
officialOwnShare.formula: Citations matched to our official sites / all citations x 100 (counted by citations, not domains)

ownedHitRate.definition: Share of measured prompts that cite an owned URL (the registered base address and its sub-pages, target URLs included) at least once. Judged per prompt, so its denominator differs from the answer-level citation metrics; it shares the same denominator as the Target URL Hit Rate beside it (owned is a superset of target). The Official Citation Rate in the published citation reports is answer-level, so its denominator differs from this one. Not computed while a source-category filter is active (the classification is derived per citation and cannot be combined with prompt-level judgment).
ownedHitRate.formula: Prompts citing an owned URL / measured prompts x 100 (multiple citations within one prompt count once)

targetHitRate.definition: Share of measured prompts whose own designated target page was actually cited. It asks whether the intended page was reached, not merely whether the site was cited. Judged per prompt, so its denominator differs from the answer-level citation metrics; it matches the Target URL Hit Rate in the published citation reports. A hit requires the addresses to be identical after normalization (protocol, www, trailing slash and tracking parameters removed) — the same rule the reports use. Not computed while a source-category filter is active (the classification is derived per citation and cannot be combined with prompt-level judgment).
targetHitRate.formula: Prompts whose target URL was cited / measured prompts x 100 (a hit on another prompt's target does not count)

states.nositeDesc: AI Visibility is built from the search impressions (Search Console) and AI crawls (server access logs) of site pages. No site is connected in your account's scope yet; this screen fills in once collection is connected.

seo.d: How many times a page appeared in search results (Google Search Console impressions).
seo.f: Sum of the daily impressions by device

ai.d: How many times an AI engine's crawler (bot) requested the page (server access log).
ai.f: Sum of the daily requests by crawler

cov.d: The share of pages an AI crawler requested at least once in the period — how many pages AI does not see at all.
cov.f: Pages with ≥ 1 AI crawl ÷ measured pages × 100

int.d: AI crawls per 10,000 search impressions — how much AI reads relative to people's search demand.

read.d: The share of measured days with at least one AI crawl — how steadily a page is read.
read.f: Days with ≥ 1 AI crawl ÷ measured days (≥ 90% almost daily · 50–90% often · < 50% sometimes)

stale.d: Days from the last AI crawl to the last measured day of the period. 7 days or more counts as ‘not read for long’.
stale.f: Last measured day − last day with ≥ 1 AI crawl

exp.d: How many AI crawls a page would get for its search reach — the AI interest of the whole selection applied to the page. A comparison baseline, not a prediction.
exp.f: Expected = page impressions × (AI crawls ÷ impressions of the selection) · achievement = actual ÷ expected · shortfall = expected − actual (positive part)

top.d: How much AI crawling piles up on a few pages. The farther the Lorenz curve from the diagonal, the more concentrated.
top.f: AI crawls of the top 10% pages ÷ all AI crawls · Gini = 1 − 2 × area under the curve

sec.d: Pages grouped by the first URL path segment after the country / language parts (e.g. /us/en/shopping-tools/offers → /shopping-tools). An address rule, not the site's menu.
sec.f: First URL path segment (2-letter country / language segments skipped)

summary.title: This period
summary.how: The five metrics above are computed straight from per-page, per-day search impressions and AI crawls (formulas in each ⓘ). The findings below are four picked by rules from this screen's numbers — priority-1 pages not read for long, URL sections whose AI share trails their search share, pages under the baseline, engine coverage gaps, change against the previous period, concentration.

eshare.info: Each engine's share of AI crawls per 7-day block counted back from the last measured day (a shorter first block is left out). The date under a bar = the block's last day.

combo.title: Engine combinations reading each page
combo.info: For each page, the set of engines that requested it at least once in the period. A page read by one engine only can ground only that engine's answers.

esec.title: Engine × URL section coverage
esec.info: Cell = the share of the section's pages the engine read at least once. Colours are fixed bands (25 · 50 · 75 · 90%). URL section = the first path segment after the country / language parts.

bots.title: Crawlers
bots.info: Requests per crawler (bot) and its share of all. The bot-to-engine link follows the crawler reference data. The source has no bot purpose (training · search · user request), so none is shown.

bench.title: Site benchmark

secs.title: Search share vs AI share by URL section
secs.sub: Grey dot = the section's share of search impressions, navy dot = its share of AI crawls. Navy to the left means AI reads the section less than people search for it.

comp.title: Source category mix
comp.info: Citations of AI answers grouped by source category — share and count (citations, not domains). Change = vs the previous round (or the equal period just before, when a period is selected) (pp), drawn as a bar around 0 on one axis for every row (the largest change on screen, at least ±{cap}pp), so bar lengths compare. Blue = up, orange = down (direction, not good or bad). Trend = weekly share — wobbles under {span}pp are drawn nearly flat so only real trends tilt. matrix.title: Source preference matrix
matrix.infoEngine: The category mix of the sources each AI engine cited (each column sums to 100%). Number = that engine's share, colour = the gap to the All column — blue sources are cited more than average by that engine, orange less. All = the sum of the engines in the table. Columns with fewer than {min} citations stay uncoloured: the gap may be chance.
matrix.infoType: The category mix of the sources cited by answers whose mention of us carries that type signal (final choice · recommendation · comparison · definition · mention; each column sums to 100%). An answer with several signals counts in each; All = the sum of the types in the table. Colours as in the engine view; columns with fewer than {min} citations stay uncoloured.
matrix.subEngine: Blue = sources an engine relies on more than average, orange = less — an engine with an orange Official (HMG) row is the one to work on.
matrix.subType: In endorsement order (final choice → mention) — the colour of the Official (HMG) row in recommendation and final-choice answers matters most.

matrix.oneSource: One source picked, so every column is 100% — the cells show citation counts.
